target_customer: AI labs and AI dev tool startups that need expert quality coding data
problem: Training and evaluating coding LLMs needs hard, high quality data that generic labeling vendors do not supply.
business_model: data sales to model labs, with a bounty marketplace paying engineers

founders.name: Serena Ge
education: University of Waterloo, computer science, dropped out after one year

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a gamified annotation platform and quality control for coding tasks is solid engineering; the hard part is recruiting and vetting expert engineers.

defensibility.rationale: Expert network and datasets help, but larger vendors can add coding streams.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch (October 2025) names Scale, Surge and Mercor as competitors.

market_need_then: Labs were spending heavily on training data; the founders said coding LLM data was a bottleneck; dated evidence from 2024 not opened.

identity.visual_style: Brain, head, datacenter and chip imagery in the footer
identity.voice_and_tone: Ambitious and philosophical, 'Data is the DNA of the next mind'

branding.brand_signature: Shipd contributor platform with bounties, over 1 million dollars paid per TechCrunch

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive bounty hunter contributor brand Shipd, but company name carries little press on its own.

outcome_analysis: Datacurve joined YC in Winter 2024, raised a 2.7 million dollar seed and a 15 million dollar Series A in October 2025, and is growing as a data vendor to AI labs. It benefits from strong lab demand for coding data and a bounty model that attracts expert engineers, but it faces larger rivals such as Scale and Surge.
notes: Series A cross-checked by TechCrunch, Maginative and Homebrew snippet. Seed date not stated by TechCrunch. One directory lists a third co-founder; unconfirmed and omitted. Competitors are named only in 2025 coverage, so competition_at_founding is empty. Outcome search returned unrelated results.
